subject: ALLOCATE statement
notes: kb/Work PB231 (the POINTER third, 2026-09-05) CLOSES this row. The byte-window carriage gate DataBinder.ByteWindowResidueOf now has NO residue: every leaf kind reaching it is carried, so GR3's 'the amount of storage to be allocated is the number of bytes required to hold an item as described by data-name-1' is computed and observed for EVERY legal data-name-1 this compiler admits. The pointer third was the last one, and its mechanism is the only one that is not a byte layout: a class-pointer / class-object item holds a MANAGED REFERENCE, which is not a byte sequence, so it rides the same storage area's MANAGED SLOT (StorageCell.SlotAt / CobolPtr.SlotRead, addressed through Place.SlotWindow at the byte offset its RESERVED bytes occupy). The reservation is what keeps GR3 a byte quantity: 13.18.60.4 GR23 leaves the size to the implementor ('Each implementor defines the precise effect of the USAGE POINTER clause upon alignment, size, representation, and range of values of the data item in the storage of the computer') and WiseOwl COBOL pins EIGHT, so conformance:cases/14.9.3-ALLOCATE/pb231_based_pointer_leaf ALLOCATEs 01 P USAGE POINTER BASED, windows the cell through a second BASED PIC X(8) entry - a shorter cell would raise EC-BOUND-PTR at the dereference, 13.18.5.4 GR4 - and reads bytes 1 and 8 with FUNCTION ORD as 33 33 (the space) BOTH BEFORE AND AFTER the pointer is given a real address, which is the assertion that the value is not in the image while the eight bytes are still allocated. The address is proved real by dereferencing it (DEREF=[ABCD]). Two REACHABLE spellings exist and both run: 13.18.60.3 SR14's level-1 elementary arm and its 'subordinate to a type declaration that includes the STRONG phrase' arm (the golden's 01 R TYPE T-PTR BASED, whose pointer member round-trips an address beside an alphanumeric member that keeps its own content). Opening the gate would have turned TWO nonconforming shapes into clean compiles, since the residue diagnostic COBOL1695 had been rejecting them for the wrong reason, so the rules that actually bar them landed in the same change set: COBOL1797 (13.18.5.3 SR1, 'The subject of the entry shall not be of class object') and COBOL1796 (13.18.22.3 SR4, 'The EXTERNAL clause shall not be specified for a data item of class object or pointer'), witnessed by conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb231-based-object-reference and conformance:cases/13.18.22-EXTERNAL/pb231-external-pointer-item. The negative fixture pb164-based-national-leaf is DELETED - its last witness shape is now a positive golden, exactly as pb151-based-comp-leaf was retired at the PB164 landing.
